mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop below 1.2 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1200 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which typically precedes lower earnings for S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate above 4% and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a sharp labor market deterioration, which depresses consumer demand and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.0% AND PAYEMS < previous month by > 100000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 3% while personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) are flat or declining signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in economic activity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 3% AND GDPC1 <= previous month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains above 4% for three consecutive months signals a disconnect between inflation and policy rates, which may indicate an impending policy pivot and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS > 4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% for three consecutive months signals a robust residential construction cycle, which boosts demand for materials and services and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during a confirmed recession.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered non-recessionary periods.
